name: Score particles
goalName: Creating particles on a basket when a ball goes through
goal: In a meeting about game feel with expert game designers, it was pointed out that a special event should have a heavy impact on the player(s). Scoring in the basketball game is the biggest non-blocking event that can happen, so it deserves special effects. Because a game consists of video and audio and the game already has a sound when someone scores, the decision was made to add particles.

approach.text: The first thing I did was adding the particle system to the basket and look at the options that were there. While playing with the settings, I noticed that the particles were not rendering correctly. The color of the particles was set to change over time, but they did not.
I looked up why the particles were not changing colors, but I found no helpful solution.

After a while, I decided to take a second look at the settings, making a small prototype with the base settings and a color. I noticed that the renderer module had a material setting that was unset. After setting it to a default particle material, it worked. The particle system worked, so I focused on making it look better. By adding gravity and a shape to the emission, the end result looks like a ring burst.

normalLearnings: I learned particle systems need a material for colors to be applicable.
I learned how various modules of the particle system work.
result: As seen in the video , when a player scores, a ring of particles is emitted.<<video https://www.youtube.com/embed/kmGLeNAJWYo>>
validation: In the test session, the participants were happy with the result.
contribution: The particles are added to the end result to improve the game feel.
